title: Degraded-paths priority reshuffle and variant bypass policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a controlled policy to reshuffle tenant priorities and selectively bypass model-variant routing when the primary Dedicated region experiences degraded paths (network congestion, partial node degradation, or transient kernel timeouts). The goal is to keep latency SLOs for high-priority tenants while minimizing cost and preserving isolation guarantees. This ticket covers policy definition, guardrail thresholds, telemetry events, and an initial canary rollout plan.
background: We observed multiple incidents where tail latencies in a Dedicated pool rose due to transient network flaps and GPU kernel stalls. Existing spillover logic pushes requests to Hosted but doesn’t consider reshuffling tenant priority windows or bypassing expensive variant fallbacks that increase token cost. For some enterprise customers with strict cost isolation, blind spillover causes billing surprises and noisy alerts. We need a more nuanced degraded-paths policy that: 1) reorders tenant priority within the affected shard, 2) optionally bypasses heavy-model-variant demotions in favor of cheaper local variants, and 3) emits structured telemetry for post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can detect a degraded-path state using: moving-window P99 latency spike (>2x baseline) OR kernel-timeout rate > 0.5% OR egress network packet loss >0.2%
When degraded-path is active, policy can atomically reshuffle tenant priorities within the pool for the configured grace window (default 30s)

Variant bypass rules can be toggled per-tenant: when enabled, the router will avoid demoting to the most expensive fallback variants and instead use a local low-cost variant or degrade tokens with explicit consent
All policy transitions are recorded as structured events (policy_id, reason_code, snapshot_of_capacity, affected_tenants) and surfaced to the Console timeline
Automated canary rollout: 2% traffic from low-risk tenants for 48 hours without SLO regressions before expanding to staging tenants
Unit and integration tests cover priority reshuffle, bypass toggles, and graceful recovery path where state is reverted after the grace window
technical_notes: Add a policy state machine in the capacity-adjudicator component with states: NORMAL -> DEGRADED_PATH -> ESCALATED -> RECOVERING
Implement a lightweight tenant priority buffer (ring buffer) per shard to support atomic reshuffle without global locks
Introduce an econometrics flag in the routing decision: variant_bypass_score = f(tenant_priority, token_cost_delta, recent_error_rate)
Emit new telemetry metrics: policy.transition.count, policy.degraded_path.duration, routing.variant_bypass.count, tenant.priority_reshuffle.count
Guardrail: reshuffle can only move a tenant up one step in priority within a single event to avoid starvation; repeated events can move further
Store policy snapshots to the audit log for compliance when private deployments are enabled (ensure KMS-encrypted storage in Private)
UI hooks: Console should show a live indicator on affected pools with one-click rollback of active degraded-path policies for SREs
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design and proto (2 weeks) - finalize thresholds and event schema; add unit tests for state machine
Phase 2: Router changes (3 weeks) - implement priority buffer and econometrics flag; add telemetry stubs
Phase 3: Telemetry & Console (2 weeks) - surface events and add pool-level indicator; add canary controls
Phase 4: Canary & rollout (1 week) - 2% low-risk canary, monitor for SLO regressions; expand gradually
Phase 5: Post-mortem automation (1 week) - auto-generate incident notes if policy triggers and SLOs breached
risks: Aggressive reshuffle could violate tenant isolation expectations—mitigated by one-step movement and per-tenant opt-outs
Variant bypass might reduce output quality for affected tenants—require opt-in or agreement in SLA
Complexity in rollback during multi-pool incidents—add conservative default timers and centralized SRE kill-switch
Telemetry volume increase—ensure cardinality controls and sampling for high-traffic pools
qa_plan: Unit tests for policy state transitions and guardrail enforcement
Integration test harness that simulates kernel stalls, packet loss, and latency spikes to validate policy triggers
Canary monitor dashboard: track P50/P90/P99, token cost delta, variant usage, and error rates for canary tenants
Chaos test schedule: introduce synthetic faults in staging for 72h and validate automatic recovery and audit logs
